text.p: Italian bond futures held to easier levels in late trading reflecting the lower tone to many overseas bond markets and also the lira which retreated from recent highs, dealers said.

They pointed out that lower German bunds and U.S. T-bonds and the easier lira prompted some profit-taking after a strong run-up, but Italian contracts managed to find some support to finished well above the day's lows.
"There is not much to go for in the Italian market at the moment so with bunds weakening, the BTPs lost heart and paused for breath," said one trader on the LIFFE market.
LIFFE's December contract expired today, and the rolling forward of futures contracts to the new lead month of March helped give some support to the March contract.

After stumbling today, BTPs will look to other markets and the currency before another move forward. The recent dollar surge largely behind the lira's strength tailled off today as the U.S. currency held around to recent firm levels.

Dealers sees the next market focus being official November Italy's CPI data on Thursday which is expected to confirm preliminary figures which showed a dip to 2.6 percent from October's official figure of 3.0 percent.
Abroad, attention will focus on the regular Bundesbank council meeting on Thursday, and U.S. non-farm November payroll data on Friday.
